_doc: Single source of truth for the Nexus memory lifetime-axis capture partition. This machine-readable artifact encodes the same rule set that skills/nexus-memory/SKILL.md describes in prose (the 'Default rule' + Break-tie #4/#5). BOTH consume this ONE artifact: hooks/memory_capture.py loads it at runtime to decide whether to nudge nexus.memory_create, and SKILL.md references it by path. Do NOT duplicate or diverge these rules in either consumer (single-rule-set invariant, proposal D2/D5; parity enforced by the T4 test). Classification is by LIFETIME (durable cross-session vs transient within-session), never by topic. Capture iff a capture_positive pattern matches AND no transient_negative pattern matches (negative overrides — D7 / over-capture bound). All patterns are lowercase Python `re` regex evaluated against the lowercased prompt. CALIBRATION NOTES (deferred to T5 measured dogfood per D7, not blind-tightened): (a) broad reaction verbs 'i like'/'i love'/'i work' can over-fire on transient usage ('I like that approach for this file') — kept because they also carry genuine durable preferences; tighten only if T5 measures real over-capture. (b) trailing '?' is a HARD ignore (questions are usually recalls) — it will silence the occasional question-framed durable write by design. The nudge is advisory + self-bounded (it tells Claude to skip if transient), so false positives cannot force a write.
